co_ridge_4.blurb: Ridge 4 is one of the numbered cliffs on Eldorado Mountain, just south of Eldorado Canyon near Boulder. The fine-grained sandstone is covered in edges, flakes and corners, and the walls look south. Nearly all of the 19 routes are bolted, with two trad lines mixed in. The grading runs steep: mostly 5.11 and 5.12, two 5.13s, and just one easy route around 5.6. Lines reach about 80 feet. A faint path climbs through grass, forest and a talus field to reach the bolted overhangs. It sees little traffic compared with the famous canyon walls.

co_big_thompson_canyon_ice.blurb: These winter flows hang beside US 34 between Loveland and Estes Park, at roughly 6,700 feet. The ice sits fairly high on a south-facing hillside and the walk in is short and easy, although getting across the river is the hard part until it freezes solid. Of the 19 lines, most are WI2 or WI3, with one WI4, a couple of WI5s and a single M4 mixed line. That moderate spread makes it a friendly place to learn ice or take first leads. Two distinct pitches form reliably; it is mainly a local-weekend venue.

co_03_machine_gun_kelly.blurb: Machine Gun Kelly is a loosely defined stretch of limestone cliff on the north side of The Bank, part of Shelf Road near Cañon City. It lies between the Bank Rob wall and its neighbour to the right. All 19 routes are bolted sport lines, with an overhanging section. Grades are mostly 5.10 and 5.11, with a handful of 5.8 and 5.9 lines, two 5.12s and one easy 5.5. The face has no standout feature, but several of the lines are well worth doing. Walk along the base past Bank Rob, or traverse left from the 2150 Wall.

co_aretes.blurb: Aretes is a trad wall on the North Rim of the Black Canyon of the Gunnison, between the Painted Wall and SOB Gully. Reach it by dropping down SOB Gully almost to the river and finding gullies on the downstream side. The climbs are long, serious multi-pitch lines, from roughly 500 to 1,900 feet and 5 to 18 pitches, so route-finding skill matters and broken rock turns up now and then. Of the 19 routes, most are 5.10 and 5.11, with a few 5.12s and only a couple of easier ones. Expect adventure climbing with gear, not bolts.

co_02_bank_rob.blurb: Bank Rob is a popular limestone wall on the north side of The Bank at Shelf Road, outside Cañon City, sitting between the Piggy Bank wall and Machine Gun Kelly. It holds 19 routes, mostly sport with two trad lines. Grades are friendly: the left end has short 5.5 to 5.7 climbs that suit kids and beginners, while the right end packs in many 5.8 to 5.10 routes, topping out at a single 5.11. From the Bank parking area, follow the dirt road for around ten minutes, then take the trail signed for Piggy Bank to reach the base.

co_devil_s_gate.blurb: Devil's Gate is a granite crag in the Devil's Gate Sector of Devil's Head, in Colorado's South Platte country. The rock is red and patinated, and the wall is slightly overhung and continuous, so the pump builds fast with few spots to rest. It holds 19 routes: 15 sport and four trad. The grades lean hard, with seven at 5.12 and four at 5.11, though a few 5.8 and 5.9 climbs and one 5.6 give lower-grade options. The cliff stands right beside the main sector trail, and the walk up takes roughly half an hour.

co_lower_mighty_mouse_wall.blurb: Lower Mighty Mouse Wall is the bottom half of a cliff on the south side of Highway 141 in Unaweep Canyon, in the Grand Junction area. A bushy break divides it from the upper wall. All 19 routes are trad, a few of them also bolted for sport, mostly 5.8 to 5.10 with two 5.11s and two 5.7s. The wall faces north and sits in morning shade, and you can follow the shade through the day. Quiet and lightly travelled, so watch for loose rock. A cairned path crosses BLM ground to reach the base.

_conflicts.co_devil_s_gate: Stored aspect E, but https://www.mountainproject.com/area/110344938/devils-gate says the wall gets sun mid to late afternoon (a western exposure).
_conflicts.co_lower_mighty_mouse_wall: Stored rock sandstone, but https://www.mountainproject.com/area/106475253/lower-mighty-mouse-wall breadcrumb names Unaweep granite and the canyon cliffs are described as granite/gneiss (https://www.visitgrandjunction.com/blog/post/unaweep-canyon-the-best-climbing-in-colorado/).
_conflicts.co_big_thompson_canyon_ice: Stored rock schist, but https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105744364/big-thompson-canyon describes granite and gneiss crags.
